candidates.title: Police did not intervene as Canada's most prolific voyeur was 'looking for more victims,' court records show
candidates.description: Saanich police watched but did not intervene for over a month as Canada's most prolific voyeur strode through businesses with a phone in hand while out on bail, in breach of bail conditions. Court records obtained by CBC News reveal that a Crown lawyer believed Yin Yeung Derek Chan was on the hunt for more victims in Fitness World and Value Village, where the voyeur had previously recorded hundreds of women and girls.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Man 27, charged in stabbing inside Edmonton Sikh temple
candidates.description: Nearly three weeks since two men were stabbed inside a Sikh temple in Edmonton, police have laid criminal charges in the case. Austin Sim-Pelletier, 27, has been charged with two counts of assault causing bodily harm and two counts of possession of a weapon for a dangerous purpose and mischief.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta First Nation wants to set up safe haven for gender-affirming care
candidates.description: Saddle Lake Cree Nation says its aiming to defy Premier Danielle Smith's government by establishing a safe haven for gender-affirming care. Chief Dale Steinhauer described the law as dehumanizing and says health care is protected under treaty rights.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Soaring licence costs drive fishermen into questionable financing deals
candidates.description: Fishing associations are concerned that the independence and profitability of Atlantic inshore fishing are at risk because of where fishermen are getting the money they need to operate.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Shelter in place order into 2nd day in Deep River after woman stabbed
candidates.description: Residents of Deep River, Ont., have been told to shelter in place as a precaution following a stabbing Wednesday evening that left one person with life-threatening injuries, according to provincial police. No arrests have been announced.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Business owners say Regina's tent encampment is hurting neighbourhood
candidates.description: The encampment in Pepsi Park has been steadily growing this summer, now reaching 70 tents and some 150 people. The city has moved to an outreach approach, rather than dismantling it. While some advocates call for more supports like showers and electricity, business owners say it's costing them.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: N.L. residents helped Muslims feel safe amid post-9/11 prejudice, says association leader
candidates.description: Twenty-five years after the Sept. 11 attacks on New York in 2001, the head of Newfoundland and Labrador's Muslim association says he looks back on the day with shock. However, Haseen Khan said communities rallied together in the years that followed to ensure support for Muslims in the province.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Injured workers could lose key protection under proposed Ontario bill, advocates warn
candidates.description: A proposed Ontario bill could strip away a key protection for people who sustained long-term injuries at work, some advocates warn.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New report highlights how some N.S. students with disabilities are excluded at school
candidates.description: A new report by Inclusion Nova Scotia highlights the ways in which some students are being excluded from their peers at school because of their disabilities. Nova Scotia's education minister says the province is already working on some of the report's recommendations.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hamilton man who shared actions online pleads guilty to drugging, sexually assaulting 2 more women
candidates.description: A Hamilton man has pleaded guilty to drugging and sexually assaulting two more women in a case that involved him recording and posting his actions online. Bryan Hayward, 37, pleaded guilty in June to seven counts. On Sept. 4, he pleaded guilty to charges involving two more women. He's also set for a Calgary trial in November.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's big banks embrace AI as workers face job uncertainty
candidates.description: According to a study by Toronto Metropolitan University, 98 per cent of financial sector workers are highly exposed to AI technologies. However, at least one Canadian bank still expects its staff levels to rise.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian citizenship certificate applications now facing nearly 3-year delays
candidates.description: Less than nine months after Parliament allowed those with Canadian ancestors to be recognized as Canadian citizens, the backlog of applications has soared to a new high.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ontario court records accessed in cybersecurity breach
candidates.description: The personal information of people involved in Ontario's court systems may have been stolen in a cyber attack, according to the chief justices of the province. An online case management system used by the courts and owned by Thomson Reuters Canada Limited was breached in June.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: N.B. producers will feel the squeeze of U.S. ban on certain Canadian goods
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump's new trade sanctions will hit home for some New Brunswick businesses. Moosehead Breweries and Mother Mushroom Brewery on Campobello Island both rely on U.S. beer drinkers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Barry Melrose, former NHL player-turned-coach and broadcaster, dead at 70
candidates.description: Barry Melrose, a hockey player-turned-coach who led the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final before going on to a long career in broadcasting the sport, has died. He was 70.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Human Rights Tribunal orders B.C. doctor to pay after refusing to provide trans teen with puberty blocker shot
candidates.description: A B.C. family doctor has been ordered to pay $28,100, after refusing to inject a transgender teen with a prescribed hormone blocker, citing religious and cultural reasons.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'What did they do to Cole Caufield?' Gamers roast new NHL game over inaccurate face scans
candidates.description: NHL 27, the new hockey simulation video game by EA Sports, launches worldwide on Sept. 11, but fans say the players’ faces are all wrong after images were leaked online.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: RCMP officer who broke Sask. hospital patient's arm won't be charged
candidates.description: Saskatchewan's Serious Incident Response Team found "reasonable grounds" to believe the officer committed assault causing bodily harm on a 38-year-old woman outside Melfort Hospital during an arrest, but the province has declined to pursue a charge.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Liberals remove layer of review process for energy projects, backing off bypassing at-risk species protections
candidates.description: The federal government is moving ahead with changes that will exempt a number of energy projects from a layer of its environmental assessment process. At the same time, a senior government source says the Liberals are preparing to back down on proposed changes that would have bypassed regulations meant to protect at-risk species.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: AC/DC concert at Rogers Stadium in Toronto cancelled due to 'severe' storm damage: Live Nation
candidates.description: Live Nation says an AC/DC concert scheduled for Sept. 16 at Rogers Stadium has been cancelled due to severe damage done to the venue by a storm a week ago.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: No longer taboo, Canada's defence industry steps into Europe's spotlight
candidates.description: At Poland's massive MSPO arms fair, Canada arrives as the 'lead nation' with 230 firms. But shifting decades of reliance on the American market won't be easy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada, Ukraine forge 100-year pact built on drones and defence
candidates.description: Canada and Ukraine signed a sweeping 100-year partnership on Thursday that puts defence production at its core. Ottawa plans to build millions of drones, pairing Canadian firms with Ukraine's battle-tested industry, while expanding co-operation on counter-drone technology, munitions and AI. Canada also pledged new funding for air defence and energy security.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Kimmel says interview with Democratic candidate won't air on his network show, cites FCC threats
candidates.description: ABC late-night talk show host Jimmy Kimmel said an interview with Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico on Thursday will air on YouTube and not during the network broadcast, citing threats from the ‌Federal Communications Commission.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 25 people killed in commercial ship fire in China
candidates.description: Twenty-five people died in a fire aboard a foreign cargo vessel undergoing repairs at a state-owned ‌shipyard in the eastern Chinese city of Qingdao on Thursday, state media reported.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump offers $5,000 US to every American if Republicans win midterm elections
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Wednesday he would pay every American adult a $5,000 US "Trump dividend" if Republicans retain control of Congress in November's midterm elections, an extraordinary attempt to persuade voters to back his party.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Sinkhole swallows driveway of Malibu mansion reportedly owned by Nicolas Cage
candidates.description: The driveway of a coastal mansion in Malibu believed to belong to Nicolas Cage collapsed Tuesday morning as a giant sinkhole opened up in front of the home.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Renewed U.S.-Iran exchanges send oil price back over $100 US for first time in several weeks
candidates.description: Iran said Wednesday it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, with the attacks ‌in and around the vital waterway sending the international Brent crude benchmark over $100 US a barrel for the first time since July.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Pilot of Amazon plane flagged excessive speed before deadly Miami crash, investigators say
candidates.description: One of the pilots of the Amazon cargo plane that careened off a Miami runway and killed five people repeatedly warned they were coming in too fast nearly two minutes ahead of time and at the last second urged them to abort the landing, according to highlights of the cockpit recording that investigators released Wednesday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Fire on passenger ferry in Philippines leaves at least 5 dead, dozens missing
candidates.description: Rescuers struggled on Thursday to get into a passenger ferry that had caught fire and burned overnight off the western Philippines, leaving five people dead and 86 missing, officials said. By nightfall, search and rescue operations were halted but were to resume in the morning.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrives in Canada
candidates.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is in Canada this week for his first visit to the country in nearly a year as his country copes with an onslaught of deadly airstrikes.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: AI researchers 'earnestly believe' it could kill all humans within the next decade, Anthropic employee says
candidates.description: There is a more than 10 per cent chance that AI could kill all humans within the next decade, a researcher at Anthropic estimated in a post, hours after social media posts went viral from someone saying they had just quit Anthropic over concerns that AI companies are “gambling with our lives” in the AI development race.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Apple unveils iPhone Duo, its new folding phone that costs at least $3K
candidates.description: Apple on Wednesday unveiled a foldable phone called Duo, introducing the biggest change in years in the company's flagship product.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Can Canada actually win a trade war with the U.S.? | About That
candidates.description: How can Canada win a trade war with the U.S. when leverage isn't equal? Andrew Chang explains how Canada is retaliating against massive tariffs levied by a neighbour 13 times its economic size. (Photo credits: The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images)
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ex-Doctor Who actor Noel Clarke charged with several sexual offences including assault, voyeurism
candidates.description: Noel Clarke, best known for his role in the sci-fi show Doctor Who from 2005 to 2010, has been charged with six sexual offences, including two counts of sexual assault, England and Wales’ Crown Prosecution Service announced on Wednesday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: South Park pulls a Trump, to be renamed South America for new season
candidates.description: South Park appears to be taking a page out of Donald Trump's book: if you don’t like a name, change it. For its 29th season, the animated satire has announced a new title — and will be now known as South America.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: China says it held 'candid and in-depth' military talks with Canadian officials last week
candidates.description: As the Carney government pursues deeper relations with Beijing, the Chinese government reports it held a "candid" exchange on military issues with Canadian officials earlier this month.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Bangladesh in grips of world's worst measles outbreak, with 1,000 dead in last 6 months
candidates.description: Bangladesh, which once came close to eliminating measles, is facing its worst outbreak on record, with around 1,000 suspected and confirmed measles-related deaths reported since March as hospitals struggle with overcrowding, shortages and a continuing influx of sick children.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Drones a key part of Nepal's response to flash-flood disaster
candidates.description: With roads and bridges destroyed and helicopters busy with search and rescue operations after last month's devastating floods, Nepal's army is turning to drones to ‌deliver relief to displaced people.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Unhinged' for Canada to call dispute with U.S. a trade war, says Trump's tariff chief
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump's top trade official says it's "unhinged" for Canadian leaders to characterize the administration's tariffs as a trade war against Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What will Trump's retaliatory tariffs do to Canada’s economy big picture? Not that much, economists predict
candidates.description: With some tariffs added and others removed, economists predict that big picture the changes will break even. But certain industries will still be hit hard, they say, and the tit-for-tat will weigh on business owners' confidence.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Apple's new iPhone Duo costs more in Canada, but not because of tariffs
candidates.description: Apple's new foldable iPhone Duo is retailing for prices starting from $2,999 in Canada, before tax. In the U.S., prices start at $1,999 US, which works out as $2,760 — meaning Canadians will have to pay almost 10 per cent more for the cheapest version.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Average asking rents fall 4.8% in August as trade war adds fresh uncertainty: report
candidates.description: A monthly report from Rentals.ca and Urbanation says the August number marks the steepest year-over-year drop since March.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Yemen's Houthis reportedly seize strategic Red Sea port of Mokha
candidates.description: Mokha's capture would bring the Iran-backed group closer to controlling the Bab al-Mandab Strait waterway, a key shipping route.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Pilot warned Amazon cargo plane going too fast before deadly crash, data shows
candidates.description: One pilot told the other about the aircraft's "excessive speed" but received an uneven response even as alarms sounded.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Israel's Netanyahu to sue newspaper over claim UAE warned him of 7 October attack
candidates.description: The paper said it stood by its reporting, after publishing extracts from a book where the claim appears.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: More than 20 children feared dead in DR Congo school fire
candidates.description: Officials say there was a stampede as they fled a fire that engulfed two schools in the eastern rebel-held city of Bukavu.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Royal family rift after popular TV news presenter chosen to succeed Ugandan king
candidates.description: King Oyo's family say he left a will naming his young son as heir to the Tooro kingdom.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone
candidates.description: Apple showed off at an event the first major design change to the iPhone in almost 20 years.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Iran war won't end until after crucial November elections, says Trump
candidates.description: The president also said oil prices won't come down until after the November races, claiming without evidence that Iran wants to impact the election.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Spanish intelligence warned of Ceuta mass crossing plans before surge
candidates.description: Declassified documents show Spanish and Moroccan authorities were alerted to social media calls for a mass migrant crossing the day before tens of thousands entered Ceuta.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Muted US response to UK's West Bank sanctions may reflect simmering frustration
candidates.description: The UK accuses Israel's government of turning a blind eye to the "ethnic cleansing" of Palestinians by settlers.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Five dead and 86 missing as 'heartbreaking' fire breaks out on Philippines ferry
candidates.description: The fire broke out as the vessel nearing its destination at the tourist hotspot of Coron in Palawan.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'We never recovered him': Quest to identify remains from Ground Zero continues
candidates.description: Since the attacks, New York officials are working with new, complex technology to find traces of more than 1,000 victims.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Four key takeaways from Republican midterms convention
candidates.description: The US president covered many of the subjects he has returned to time and again - with a few surprises thrown in.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'People were trampling me': Philippine ferry fire survivor recalls narrow escape
candidates.description: A survivor has told the BBC of the chaos onboard as the ferry caught fire near the popular tourist spot of Coron.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Is Trump's $5,000 election pledge legal?
candidates.description: The US president has said every American will get $5,000 (£3,700) if the Republican Party wins November's midterms.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: How a community living under demolition orders from Israel view UK sanctions
candidates.description: Middle East Correspondent Lucy Williamson visits the Palestinian community of Khan al Ahmar, and the neighbouring Israeli settlement of Maale Admumim.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Do Republicans blame Trump for high oil prices?
candidates.description: The BBC's Sarah Smith is at the Republican Party's first midterms convention in Texas, taking place as oil prices rise to $100 (£74) a barrel.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Inside Thailand's school shooter drills following recent attacks
candidates.description: Police say they hope the drill will help prepare students, as concern grows over the increase in school shootings in South East Asia.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Norway bids farewell to King Harald
candidates.description: Tens of thousands of people lined the streets to pay their respects after 13 days of national mourning.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'
candidates.description: It is the latest in a series of increasing warnings about the safety threat posed by artificial intelligence.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Meta continues to run ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India - report
candidates.description: The report follows a BBC Eye investigation that found Instagram running paid ads promoting such material in India.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Downed trees and flooding as Hurricane Lowell batters western Hawaii
candidates.description: The storm brought damaging winds and torrential rain to parts of the island on Monday and Tuesday, triggering concerns about flash flooding and mudslides.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem
candidates.description: A curious online row over this summer's heatwaves points to a wider - and worrying - shift in climate science.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Drax ash mound extraction plan approved
candidates.description: Plans to extract and reuse million tonnes of ash from a mound next to Drax are given the go-ahead.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Backshall backs calls for natural history GCSE
candidates.description: Steve Backshall calls for nature education as a survey says 55% of children have not climbed a tree.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
candidates.description: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: UN peacekeepers give NPR a rare look behind Israeli lines
candidates.description: NPR accompanies UN peacekeepers behind Israeli lines as Israel expands its occupation of South Lebanon following a U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 'I'll never trust them again': Some Afghans who helped the U.S. post-9/11 regret it
candidates.description: Soon after the Sept. 11 attacks, the U.S. launched what would become a 20-year war in Afghanistan. Some Afghans who helped the U.S. prosecute that war regret it.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: After 900 years, the Bayeux Tapestry returns to England and goes on display in London
candidates.description: The nearly 230-foot long Bayeux Tapestry is back in England for the first time in 900 years. It depicts the 1066 Battle of Hastings, a turning point in English history that ended Anglo-Saxon rule.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Greetings from Paris, where the 2024 Olympics balloon rises again
candidates.description: The floating Olympic cauldron, held aloft by a giant glowing balloon, is still making regular appearances two years after the 2024 Paris Games, showing up all summer long in the nighttime Paris sky.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. military destroys 5 Iranian oil tankers. And, the Smithsonian head resigns
candidates.description: The U.S. military says it has destroyed five Iranian oil tankers as the conflict continues to escalate. And, Smithsonian head Lonnie G. Bunch III says he plans to step down by the end of the year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Citing the 'Deep State,' Trump overhauls the intelligence community
candidates.description: The catastrophic 9/11 attacks forced the intelligence community to radically revamp its ways of doing business. Now, critics say, President Trump is dismantling much of what was built since then.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Iceland summons U.S. ambassador after Trump posts countries draped with American flag
candidates.description: Iceland summoned the U.S. ambassador after President Trump posted a map on Truth Social that showed the country, along with a number of other nations, covered with an American flag.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. military says it destroyed 5 Iranian oil tankers after attacks on Navy warship
candidates.description: The U.S. military said it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to the latest attacks on its warships. Iran hit American targets in Jordan.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Fold the phone: Apple's new CEO unveils a foldable iPhone
candidates.description: New Apple CEO John Ternus announces the iPhone Duo, which folds like a passport and is the most radical iPhone design update in nearly 20 years.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A new Anthropic model seeks to test how AI could impact the U.S. economy
candidates.description: Will artificial intelligence nibble around the edges of the economy or upend it altogether? A new, interactive model from Anthropic lets people tests their assumptions.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 'I've never seen anything like this' -- A U.S. doctor treats Ebola's youngest victims
candidates.description: Dr. Rupa Narra is a U.S. pediatrician who arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo to help care for stricken children. Nothing could have prepared her for what she'd face.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Special education head at Education Department abruptly resigns
candidates.description: The leader of the Education Department's special education office told employees she is resigning after less than four months in the role and as the agency overall is morphing and shrinking.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Whatever happened to the measles outbreak that shocked a country this year?
candidates.description: Bangladesh has seen over 50,000 confirmed or suspected cases of measles this year. The death toll among children just surpassed 1,000. How are officials trying to bring the outbreak under control?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How to fight with the people we care about, illustrated
candidates.description: Arguing with a partner or a loved one can be anxiety-inducing. Conflict resolution facilitator Priya Parker explains how to start and end a fight — while easing dread for everyone.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A Louisiana case could upend telehealth abortion. What exactly is it?
candidates.description: As a federal appeals court considers Louisiana's lawsuit to end telehealth abortion access, a longtime OB-GYN in Arizona explains how telehealth works in his clinic.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 10 at 2:07PM CDT by NWS Chicago IL
candidates.description: Atmospheric conditions are favorable for the development of funnel clouds. These funnel clouds normally only protrude a few hundred feet downward from the parent cloud, rotate or spin like a top, and last a few minutes before dissipating. These funnel clouds rarely touch the ground and typically do not pose any sort of hazard. The atmospheric conditions that these funnel clouds develop in do not support strong, damaging tornadoes. However, on extremely rare occasions, these funnels can briefly touch the ground and produce very minimal, if any, damage. If threatening weather approaches, move indoors to a place of safety. The National Weather Service will continue to closely monitor the situation.

For the Wind Advisory, from 11 AM Saturday to 2 AM PDT Sunday. * IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result. Strong winds and rough waves on area lakes will create hazardous conditions for small craft. Blowing dust may reduce visibilities. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will increase Saturday through the morning and afternoon hours, with the strongest winds expected Saturday evening.
candidates.author: National Weather Service

candidates.title: IdeaAMBIG: Benchmarking Implementation-Critical Gaps in Research-Idea Specifications
candidates.description: A research idea may be novel, coherent, and scientifically plausible, yet its proposed method may remain insufficiently specified for faithful implementation. We study the codification readiness of implementation-facing research-method specifications, defined by whether they provide sufficient methodological information for a competent implementer or coding agent to construct the intended method without unsupported assumptions. We construct evidence-grounded specifications and their supported resolutions from papers, codebases, issue threads, and reproduction artifacts. We introduce IdeaAMBIG, a benchmark of 660 evidence-grounded instances: 163 real-world gaps from reproducibility reports and GitHub issues, and 497 controlled synthetic gaps injected into codification-ready references. IdeaAMBIG evaluates three capabilities: codification-readiness assessment, defect localization, and clarification action generation. Defect localization receives only the specification, whereas clarification additionally receives the annotated defect. Across 13 LLMs, the best model achieves 9.6% Macro Defect Recovery Rate on real-world instances but 80.6% Macro Clarification Action Success Rate when given the defect. In an oracle study, supplying the gold resolution raises the downstream codification-ready rate from 14% to 98%. Across all evaluated models, defect localization is the main bottleneck, with stronger clarification given the defect.
candidates.author: Yiling Ma, Yilun Zhao, Sihong Wu, Manasi Patwardhan, Arman Cohan

candidates.title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
candidates.description: Foundation vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit broad intelligence about the world, yet translating this intelligence into robot control remains challenging. We present Show-Harness, an Embodied Harness that enables VLMs to "play" robots through a compact semantic interface linking intent to action. Show-Harness exposes discrete semantic action units that VLMs can naturally reason over, while embodiment-specific interpreters deterministically ground them into local robot actions, keeping the VLM directly responsible for fine-grained physical decisions. Through the same interface, Show-Harness demonstrates the feasibility of (1) directly unlocking closed-source frontier VLMs for zero-shot robot control, and (2) adapting small-scale open-source VLMs for low-cost deployment with just a few GPU-hours of fine-tuning. We further develop GUMI (GUI Manipulation Interface), which extends the same semantic action space to GUI-based demonstration collection, allowing humans and agents to "play" robots across embodiments without specialized teleoperation hardware. Extensive experiments show that Show-Harness-equipped VLM agents generalize robustly across tasks, embodiments, and environments, outperforming representative agentic and VLA paradigms. These results suggest that the right interface can unlock substantial embodied capability from foundation VLMs, without requiring additional model capacity or costly embodiment-specific pretraining.
candidates.author: Yanzhe Chen, Zechen Bai, Zhijun Cao, Wenzheng Zeng, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Yiqi Lin, Guoqiang Liang, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Qiming Huang, Mike Zheng Shou

candidates.title: DUET-DINO: Simultaneous Cross-View World Modeling for Latent Planning in Robot Manipulation
candidates.description: Action-conditioned latent world models predict future visual representations, enabling zero-shot goal-conditioned robot planning and control. However, their predictions for fine-grained spatial and rotational actions are unreliable for full 7-DoF end-effector control. To address this gap, we introduce DUET-DINO, a simultaneous cross-view latent world model that jointly learns action-conditioned predictions from static side- and wrist-camera observations through cross-view conditioning. By exploiting complementary global scene and gripper-centric information, DUET-DINO enables latent planning over the full 7-DoF action space. Across spatially diverse reach, orientation-intensive angled-reach, and multi-goal grasp-and-lift tasks, DUET-DINO consistently outperforms single-view and independent dual-view baselines, achieving 92% success on reach, 72.5% on angled-reach, and 60.0% on lift tasks. DUET-DINO is trained from scratch on DROID and RoboArena datasets and generalizes robustly under visual distribution shifts. We further show that while V-JEPA 2 wrist-view predictions underestimate visual dynamics induced by fine-grained actions, DINOv3 predictions better capture action-conditioned scene changes, leading to stronger downstream planning. The code and model checkpoints will be open-sourced. Project page: https://utn-air.github.io/DUET-DINO
candidates.author: Nisarga Nilavadi, Ralf Römer, Moritz Reuss, Michael Krawez, Tobias Jülg, Angela P. Schoellig, Rudolf Lioutikov, Wolfram Burgard

candidates.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
candidates.description: Enterprises deploy systems, not checkpoints. Usable capability depends jointly on weights, serving route, precision, output contract, and harness, yet all 18 audited benchmarks score advertised model identifiers. We treat this as measurement error and give a protocol that makes it reportable. It has three parts. A gold-blind capability-binding preflight verifies that a route can execute the evaluation contract before any task reaches it; a reliability-inclusive first-pass scoring rule keeps failure in the score while keeping unsupported capability out; and adjudication is structurally score-blind. We call the protocol IB2 and release its algorithms, classification tables, request contract, and manifest schemas. Its reference instantiation, 128 locked tasks and 987 assertions over document, spreadsheet, chart, tool and database work, stays sealed: the procedure is the artifact, not the corpus. Across eleven systems, four results. Capability availability is measurable: two complete single-route runs on identical weights later failed distinct predicates of the finalized binding gate, while a third passed that gate before a fresh run. The advertised identifier exposed neither limit. Discrimination is not uniform: four of seven suites saturate under a six-system band, with the spread almost entirely from governed database work and multi-tab joins, so we report interval-backed resolution groups, not ranks; two of the nominal five-label output's four cuts fail multiplicity adjustment. Serving-arm choice moved one declared revision and precision from 77.38 to 82.54, paired interval [0.11,10.60], though the arms differ in access mode, harness generation, and the serving tool-call parser, and harness generation is a property of our evaluator, not any endpoint. Excluding failed responses from denominators changes the point ordering, so reliability inclusion changes a conclusion, not its wording.
candidates.author: Blake Stenstrom, Charangan Vasantharajan, Brian Sathianathan

candidates.title: Coastal Environment Generation with HoloOcean
candidates.description: Marine robotic simulation provides a safe and inexpensive method of developing and testing algorithms for unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) and unmanned surface vessel (USV) autonomy and perception before full field deployment. However, these simulations are often limited by the availability of simulated environments. Current marine robotics simulation suites offer manual ways to edit or create environments, but they require existing data or specialized knowledge of the environment system. To address these issues, we introduce a novel Unreal Engine 5 level generation pipeline that enables automatic creation of coastal environments for HoloOcean. Our pipeline relies on a user-provided overhead image of a coastal scene. The pipeline then uses the image to generate height map data, as well as automatically select assets and place them in the environment.
candidates.author: Abigail Austin, Brady Moon, Joshua G. Mangelson

candidates.title: Semigroup-JEPA: Latent Dynamics Consistency for Zero-Shot Physics Generalization
candidates.description: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models learn a compact latent representation of the world that supports prediction and planning, but their capability to learn physics and generate physically realistic dynamics remains hitherto untested. In this work, we introduce SemiGroup-JEPA (SG-JEPA), which extends the LeWorldModel framework by supplying the parameter governing the physics to the temporal model via action-conditioning and jointly training an encoder and predictor through an autoregressive latent rollout. To evaluate the model's ability to generalize out of distribution, we design dynamical tasks under different gravitational fields that, despite obeying the same physical law, exhibit qualitatively different dynamics, ranging from floating motion in weak gravitational fields to rapid bouncing in strong ones. In contrast to DINO-WM, SG-JEPA reduces open-loop prediction error by up to 2 times on two-dimensional datasets, and increases control success rate up to 2.5 times for three-dimensional robotic datasets, for which we train independent diffusion policies. To explain this advantage, we develop a linear feature model that separates local law-conditioned error from its recursive amplification under rollout. Guided by this model, we find that back-propagating the multi-step rollout loss into the representation trains the encoder to keep the features that the predictor can carry forward, and that those are the features the dynamics depend on, so most of the gain comes from the encoder learning better features rather than from the predictor learning better dynamics. See project page at https://sg-jepa.github.io.
candidates.author: Andy Zeyi Liu, Haoran Sun, Lucas Baker, Randall Balestriero, John Sous

candidates.title: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
candidates.description: Real-world GUI usage frequently involves workflows that span multiple devices and platforms, requiring the transfer of intermediate results, maintenance of shared state, and coordination across heterogeneous environments. However, existing GUI benchmarks overwhelmingly evaluate agents on single-device, statically defined tasks, thus leaving such cross-device capabilities largely unexamined, resulting in an overly optimistic assessment of agents' readiness for real-world usage. We introduce JarvisGUI, a dynamic benchmark that evaluates GUI agents on cross-device workflows requiring coordinated interaction across heterogeneous platforms, including Android, Windows, and Ubuntu. Specifically, JarvisGUI formulates GUI tasks as input-output transformations under a lightweight type system, which allows us to automatically compose multi-step, cross-device workflows and dynamically evaluate agent performance within a unified framework. By evaluating agents in virtual environments spanning multiple operating systems, JarvisGUI reveals that state-of-the-art open-source GUI agents struggle with the state-transfer awareness, cross-platform contextual reasoning, and long-horizon dependency management required for real-world workflows, exposing a critical capability gap invisible to existing benchmarks.
candidates.author: Zixiang Chen, Yuheng Lu, Zihao Cheng, Zeming Liu, Jizeng Bai, Ziye Huang, Zhiyin Lin, Zihan Li, Yuhang Guo, Yunhong Wang, Haifeng Wang

candidates.title: Building Multilingual Bridges: Data Mixing as the Pillar of Generalization for In-Language Reasoning
candidates.description: Reasoning language models have made substantial advances on a variety of complex tasks, yet their capabilities remain overwhelmingly English-centric: models primarily reason in English regardless of the language they are prompted in. This is inaccessible for non-English-speaking users, risks losing the intent of the original question, and forgoes knowledge more readily expressed in the target language. In this work, we advance L2 reasoning, the ability of a model to reason consistently in the language of the user's prompt, thus building an in-language bridge between the prompt and the answer. We approach this problem from a data-centric angle, investigating how to optimize data composition and scheduling in SFT for reasoning generalization. Building Tiny Aya L2-Thinker at 3.35B scale, we achieve an L2 reasoning rate above 93% across 60 languages on 6 benchmarks spanning math, commonsense reasoning, instruction following, open-ended generation, and cultural reasoning while keeping performance strong. We show the path to generalizing L2 reasoning to held-out languages goes through broader language coverage, readily available multilingual non-reasoning data, and a sufficient English reasoning backbone. These findings indicate that reasoning is a language-agnostic behavior that can be transferred across typologically diverse languages through careful data mixing and without requiring reasoning supervision in every target language. We release our model weights and multilingual reasoning data to support further research on accessible, in-language reasoning.
candidates.author: Mehrnaz Mofakhami, Ananya Sahu, Alejandro R. Salamanca, Daniel D'souza, Alexandre Berard, Thomas Euyang, Marzieh Fadaee, Julia Kreutzer

candidates.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
candidates.description: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities, they often struggle with extremely long contexts due to fixed context limits. To address this, sequential approaches like MemAgent extend the effective context by reading text in segments and iteratively updating a fixed-size memory. However, this sequential paradigm suffers from high latency and requires costly reinforcement learning (RL) training, which can lead to overfitting on specific datasets. To overcome these limitations, we propose ConvMem, a training-free, highly parallelizable framework that reformulates long-context reasoning as a hierarchical convolution. Inspired by CNNs, ConvMem treats an LLM prompted with a specific query as a convolutional kernel. This kernel summarizes text segments hierarchically, shortening the reasoning path from a linear chain into a logarithmic tree. Specifically, ConvMem integrates \textit{Configurable Strides} and \textit{Skip Connections} to ensure robust evidence capture and propagation, while employing \textit{Multi-Kernel Convolution} to decompose complex queries into disentangled semantic channels. This design not only mitigates error accumulation but also enables massive parallelization across both text segments and reasoning threads. Experiments on RULER-HotpotQA and RULER-2WikiMultiHopQA demonstrate that ConvMem outperforms training-free baselines and avoids the risk of overfitting to parametric priors often observed in RL-trained models on out-of-distribution tasks.
candidates.author: Hongming Zhang, Zhaozhen Gu, Fengshuo Bai, Ming Hao, Qingyang Zhang, Yuanyuan Wang, Shiyang Tang, Yanna Wang, Bo Xu

candidates.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
candidates.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) can memorize and reproduce sensitive, copyrighted, or otherwise undesirable training content, creating privacy, safety, and regulatory concerns. Machine unlearning offers a practical alternative to full retraining, but many existing methods apply broad or fixed parameter updates that can degrade utility and remain brittle under deployment changes such as post-training quantization, where forgotten knowledge may partially re-emerge. We propose Forgetting Only What Matters via Unlearning Layers (FOM-UL), a layer-level unlearning framework that selects transformer layers using a forget-to-retain significance score. This score identifies layers with high influence on the forget set and low sensitivity to the retain set, allowing FOM-UL to concentrate updates where they are most effective while leaving most of the model unchanged. This targeted update strategy improves the forgetting-utility trade-off and provides an empirical path toward quantization-resilient unlearning by reducing the chance that small, diffuse updates are erased by low-bit rounding. Across TOFU, KnowUnDo, and MUSE-style evaluations, FOM-UL reduces residual memorization compared with strong GA, NPO, KLD, SURE, ReLearn, and LUNAR-based baselines while preserving retain-set utility close to the vanilla model. Under 8-bit and 4-bit post-training quantization, FOM-UL maintains stronger memorization suppression and utility preservation than competing methods, and adversarial prompt evaluations show lower recovery of forgotten content. Overall, FOM-UL provides an efficient unlearning strategy that improves targeted forgetting, utility preservation, and deployment robustness without claiming formal guarantees of erasure.
candidates.author: Ravi Ranjan, Olivera Kotevska, Agoritsa Polyzou

candidates.title: Do speech foundation models really learn words?
candidates.description: Self-supervised speech foundation models are now used in a wide array of downstream applications, including traditional speech recognition and as the basis for tokens in speech-aware language models. Attempts to understand their usefulness have largely focused on probing their representations' ability to discriminate phonemes and words. However, discriminative ability for words need not imply specialized representation of words per se. Good discrimination of words may be explained by good encoding of word form (phonemes) rather than form-independent word representations encoding identity or syntactic/semantic properties. By partialling out phoneme information using residualization, we show that, in later layers, HuBERT and wav2vec 2.0 do in general learn representations which encode words with reasonable fidelity independently of local phonetic content. We show that this simple approach to disentanglement can enhance higher-order linguistic information in word discovery tasks.
candidates.author: Robin Huo, Ewan Dunbar

candidates.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous UAV Exploration in Wildfire Response
candidates.description: This study develops a deep reinforcement learning framework for training Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) agents to navigate and monitor simulated wildfire environments. Results show that agents learn increasingly stable and effective behaviors over time, as demonstrated by converging loss trends, improved reward signals, and more consistent navigation patterns such as fire-boundary tracking. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based UAV systems for autonomous wildfire monitoring and suggest that environmental structure and reward design influence policy effectiveness.
candidates.author: Caden Chandra, Jerry Ng
